The study, published in the journal *Archaeological Science*, examined over 200 individuals using high‑resolution CT scanning and microscopic bone analysis to identify patterns of injury. Researchers documented a high incidence of perimortem fractures, cut marks, and projectile wounds, indicating close‑quarters fighting with swords, axes, and arrows. “It highlights the brutality of medieval warfare,” said paleopathologist Jo Buckberry, who led the investigation.

The findings suggest that combatants faced not only lethal strikes but also severe secondary trauma from falling, crushing, and battlefield debris. Comparative data from contemporary sites show similar injury distributions, reinforcing the view that medieval battles were chaotic and physically demanding. The study enhances understanding of the lived experience of soldiers in the Middle Ages and offers a scientific basis for interpreting historical accounts of medieval conflicts.
author: Ars Technica

title: Nvidia reveals $21 billion stake in SpaceX
content:
A filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission was submitted on Tuesday, following Elon Musk’s announcement that his firm had entered an exclusive arrangement to equip its data‑center infrastructure with specialized hardware. The document, filed by the technology supplier involved in the deal, outlines the terms of the partnership, the scope of equipment to be delivered, and the anticipated timeline for rollout across the company’s global data‑center network.

According to the filing, the supplier will provide a suite of high‑performance computing units, including custom‑designed processors and associated cooling solutions, to support the firm’s expanding artificial‑intelligence workloads. The agreement, described as “exclusive” and “long‑term,” is expected to enhance processing capacity while consolidating the hardware supply chain under a single vendor. The disclosure highlights projected revenue impacts for the supplier and notes that the partnership aligns with the firm’s broader strategy to increase in‑house AI capabilities. This filing formalizes the arrangement and provides investors with detailed insight into the financial and operational implications of the new data‑center initiative.
author: Ars Technica

title: Gasolini AR1 sub‑$7,000 sports car uses Honda bike engine, EV planned
content:
Gasolini has announced that its AR1 model is powered by a two‑cylinder engine sourced from a Honda motorcycle, marking a collaboration that leverages Honda’s proven small‑engine technology for the lightweight vehicle. The integration of the Honda powerplant is intended to deliver reliable performance while keeping the AR1’s overall weight and emissions low, aligning with the company’s focus on efficient, compact transportation solutions.

In parallel with the gasoline‑powered version, Gasolini is developing an electric‑vehicle (EV) iteration of the AR1. The EV project aims to replace the internal‑combustion engine with an electric drivetrain, offering a zero‑emission alternative that retains the AR1’s compact dimensions and intended use cases. Production timelines for both the Honda‑engine model and its electric counterpart have not been disclosed, but the dual‑track approach underscores Gasolini’s strategy to address diverse market demands.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon team adopts T. Rex book‑devouring logo
content:
Amazon has introduced a new logo for one of its internal teams, featuring a stylized T. Rex poised to devour a book. The image was revealed during a company‑wide briefing earlier this month and has since been adopted across the team’s internal communications, marketing collateral, and digital platforms. The design, created by Amazon’s in‑house branding studio, blends the iconic dinosaur with a classic book to underscore the team’s focus on knowledge acquisition and rapid innovation.

The logo represents the team’s mission to “devour” information and turn it into actionable insights for Amazon’s broader product ecosystem. By combining the ferocious imagery of a T. Rex with the intellectual symbolism of a book, the design signals a commitment to both speed and depth in research and development. According to the team’s lead, the visual identity was chosen to inspire a culture of curiosity and to remind members that learning is a continuous, dynamic process.

As Amazon rolls out the new branding, the team plans to integrate the logo into its internal dashboards, presentation templates, and external partner communications. The move reflects the company’s ongoing efforts to refresh its visual language and to reinforce the narrative that Amazon remains at the forefront of learning‑driven innovation.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon Uses Rare Books for AI Training
content:
Rare literary works are emerging as a strategic resource for enhancing large language models (LLMs), according to recent commentary from artificial‑intelligence researchers. While contemporary LLMs have been trained on vast corpora drawn primarily from publicly accessible digital content, many historically significant texts remain under‑represented because they have not been widely digitized or included in standard training datasets. Experts note that integrating rare books—often preserved in specialized archives and libraries—could fill gaps in cultural and scholarly knowledge, providing models with richer linguistic patterns and nuanced historical context that are absent from mainstream web sources.

Industry analysts indicate that the incorporation of these scarce materials may improve the factual depth and interpretive capabilities of future LLMs, particularly in domains such as literary criticism, historical research, and the preservation of linguistic heritage. Ongoing collaborations between AI developers and cultural institutions aim to digitize and curate rare collections for safe, licensed use in model training, balancing intellectual‑property considerations with the potential benefits of broader knowledge representation. The initiative underscores a growing recognition that expanding the diversity of source material is essential for the next generation of more comprehensive and reliable language models.
author: TechCrunch

title: Feedly blames bug for weeklong web app slowdown
content:
Feedly has identified a software bug as the cause of recent performance problems that have rendered its web application nearly unusable for a segment of its user base. The issue, which emerged in early August, triggered slow loading times, frequent timeouts, and intermittent crashes, prompting a surge of complaints on social media and user forums. In a statement released on Thursday, Feedly’s engineering team confirmed that the bug was introduced during a recent update to the platform’s content‑aggregation engine and that a fix is being rolled out to restore normal functionality.

The technical glitch coincides with growing dissatisfaction over the service’s mobile applications and customer support, which users have described as unresponsive and difficult to navigate. While the company has not disclosed specific timelines for the mobile app improvements, it has pledged to enhance its support channels and to monitor the situation closely. Feedly’s acknowledgment of the bug and its ongoing remediation efforts aim to mitigate the current disruptions and restore confidence among its subscribers.
author: TechCrunch

title: YouTube will count a view when a video starts playing
content:
YouTube has announced a new adjustment to its view‑counting methodology, a move that echoes a similar change implemented a year ago for its Shorts videos. The platform said the update will align the way views are tallied on regular uploads with the system that has already been in place for Shorts content.

Under the revised approach, YouTube will apply the same criteria and verification steps used for Shorts to all videos. This means that views will be counted only after certain thresholds are met, and the platform will employ additional checks to confirm that each view is legitimate. The change is intended to reduce inflated numbers and provide a more accurate metric for creators and advertisers.

The update reflects YouTube’s ongoing effort to improve transparency and consistency across its metrics. By standardizing view counts across all video formats, the company aims to give creators and advertisers a clearer picture of audience engagement.
author: TechCrunch

title: Sonic Fire Tech raises $15 million for sound‑powered fire protection system
content:
Sonic Fire Tech, a startup that has developed a sound‑powered fire protection system, announced the closing of a new funding round aimed at accelerating the deployment of its technology across a broad range of building types. The company’s system uses acoustic sensors to detect the early sound signatures of fire, triggering alarms and suppression measures before smoke or heat is visible.

The round, which raised an undisclosed amount, is expected to support expansion into commercial kitchens, apartment buildings, and other high‑risk environments where traditional fire detection can be delayed. Sonic Fire Tech plans to use the capital to scale production, pursue additional regulatory approvals, and broaden its marketing and sales efforts to reach more property owners and facility managers.

With the new funding, Sonic Fire Tech intends to enhance fire safety in both commercial and residential settings, providing an early‑warning system that could reduce damage and improve occupant protection across a wide range of building types.
author: TechCrunch

title: Reddit Tests Video and Audio Versions of Popular Posts
content:
Reddit has launched a test that adds video and audio formats to a selection of popular posts, giving users the option to watch or listen to content rather than solely reading text. The feature, currently being rolled out to a limited group of users, automatically generates short video clips or audio narrations from the most up‑voted submissions in various subreddits, allowing creators’ stories to be consumed in a more dynamic medium.

The experiment follows Reddit’s broader push to diversify its content offerings and increase engagement on the platform, which hosts millions of active communities. By converting text‑based posts into multimedia, Reddit aims to attract users who prefer visual or auditory consumption while maintaining the community‑driven voting system that surfaces top content. The company will monitor user feedback and interaction metrics before deciding whether to expand the feature platform‑wide.
author: TechCrunch

title: Higgsfield secures $400 million Series B funding, valuation climbs to $5.4 billion
content:
Higgsfield, a newly launched startup founded by former Snap executive Alex Mashrabov, offers a platform that enables users to create artificial‑intelligence‑generated images and videos. The company entered the market amid growing demand for consumer‑friendly tools that simplify the production of visual content using generative AI technologies.

The Higgsfield service provides an interface where users can input prompts or upload reference material to produce customized graphics and short video clips, leveraging machine‑learning models trained on large datasets. By targeting both hobbyists and professionals seeking rapid, cost‑effective content creation, the platform aims to broaden access to AI‑driven media production and compete with existing generative‑AI offerings.
author: TechCrunch

title: Spotify introduces Playlist Notes feature for users and editors
content:
Spotify has introduced a new feature that allows users to add personal commentary explaining the stories and reasoning behind their favorite tracks. The tool, integrated directly into the streaming platform, enables listeners to write brief notes that accompany songs, offering insight into lyrical meaning, cultural relevance, or personal connections.

The feature will also be employed by Spotify’s editorial team, who plan to use it on high‑profile playlists such as RapCaviar and other curated collections. By pairing editorial commentary with user‑generated notes, the service aims to deepen engagement and provide richer context for its audience while maintaining the existing playlist experience.
author: TechCrunch

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Pass Discount Up to $300 Until August 21
content:
San Francisco will host the annual Disrupt conference from October 13‑15, drawing a large segment of the startup community to Moscone West. The event, organized by TechCrunch, is scheduled to feature keynote speakers, panel discussions, and networking sessions aimed at entrepreneurs, investors, and technology professionals.

Attendees can secure their passes now, as early‑bird pricing and limited seating remain available. Registration opens immediately, and participants are encouraged to finalize their plans to ensure entry to the venue and access to all scheduled sessions. The conference will run daily from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., with a mix of in‑person and virtual components.

The next edition of Disrupt promises to showcase emerging trends in technology and venture capital, offering a platform for startups to present new products and secure funding. Those who register early will benefit from discounted rates and priority access to networking events, positioning them to engage with peers and industry leaders during the three‑day gathering.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic to add watermark to AI-generated text to meet EU regulations
content:
Anthropic announced that it will modify the way its chatbot makes small, random choices in order to meet the requirements of the European Union’s upcoming AI regulation. The company said the changes will be implemented in the next software update and are designed to increase transparency and reduce the risk of unintended bias in the model’s responses. The move comes as the EU’s AI Act moves closer to enforcement, mandating that high‑risk systems provide clear documentation of their decision‑making processes.

Key to the update is a new algorithm that limits the extent of random variation in word choice and sentence structure. Anthropic noted that typical machine‑generated tropes—such as the overuse of words like “delve,” an excess of em dashes, and the repetitive “it’s not X but Y” construction—are often a byproduct of these random choices. By tightening the randomness, the company aims to produce more consistent and less stylized output while still preserving the model’s flexibility.

With the update, Anthropic intends to demonstrate compliance with the EU’s transparency and accountability obligations, potentially setting a standard for other AI developers. The company’s statement suggests that the changes will not affect the core capabilities of the chatbot, but will instead refine its linguistic patterns to better align with regulatory expectations and user expectations for natural, varied language.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Hayden Panettiere Dies at 36; Authorities Investigate Cause
content:
Actress Hayden Panettiere, 36, was found dead earlier this week, prompting an outpouring of tributes from colleagues and fans who remembered her for roles in “Heroes,” “Nashville,” and the “Alvin and the Chipmunks” film series. Authorities have not released an official cause of death, and the investigation remains ongoing. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office confirmed that an autopsy is pending, and no details have been made public beyond the confirmation of her passing.

U.S. media outlets have reported that a dispatch audio obtained by People magazine includes a discussion among officials referencing a possible “overdose.” The report characterizes this as speculation, noting that investigators have not confirmed any substance involvement. As the case proceeds, law enforcement officials have asked for privacy for Panettiere’s family while they continue to gather facts surrounding the circumstances of her death.
author: Euronews

title: 7,200 Eggs Used to Make Giant Omelette at Malmedy Festival
content:
Volunteers gathered in Malmedy, Belgium, on Saturday to prepare a 7,200‑egg omelette as part of the annual Giant Omelette Festival. The massive dish was cooked in a four‑metre‑diameter pan set over an open fire, a tradition that draws participants and spectators from across the region each year.

Organizers reported that the omelette, which required coordinated effort from dozens of volunteers, was successfully flipped and served to festival attendees after approximately three hours of cooking. The event, promoted as a celebration of local culinary heritage, concluded with the distribution of the omelette to the public, marking another successful edition of the long‑standing Belgian festival.
author: Euronews

title: Tokyo's Fukagawa Hachiman Matsuri turns streets into water fight on Aug 16, 2026
content:
On 16 August 2026, Tokyo’s triennial Fukagawa Hachiman Matsuri turned into a splashy spectacle when crowds drenched mikoshi bearers with buckets, hoses and water pistols. The festival, held in the Fukagawa district, features a parade of portable shrines (mikoshi) that are carried through the streets by local residents and shrine attendants. During the procession, spectators lined the route and began pouring water on the bearers, creating a sudden, wet interruption to the traditional ceremony.

The incident occurred in the early afternoon, as the mikoshi made its way past the shrine’s main gate. According to police reports, the crowd’s enthusiasm led to a spontaneous water‑throwing event that lasted several minutes. No injuries were reported, and the bearers were able to continue the procession after a brief pause. Festival officials confirmed that the event did not disrupt the overall schedule, and the remaining parade proceeded as planned.

Authorities noted that the water‑throwing was an impromptu act of celebration rather than an act of vandalism. The Fukagawa Hachiman Matsuri, which attracts thousands of visitors every three years, remains a key cultural event in Tokyo, and organizers have pledged to maintain safety measures while preserving the festival’s spirited atmosphere.
author: Euronews

title: Russia Supreme Court upholds Yabloko election ban as deputy chair Lev Shlosberg receives 11-year sentence
content:
The Russian Supreme Court has confirmed the removal of the Yabloko party from the September electoral ballot after a lower court in Pskov sentenced party deputy chair Lev Shlosberg to more than eleven years in a penal colony for publicly calling for a ceasefire in the ongoing war in Ukraine.  

The Pskov court’s ruling was based on charges that Shlosberg’s statements constituted extremist propaganda and an attempt to undermine the state’s military efforts. Yabloko, a centrist opposition party, had previously announced its intention to contest the upcoming election, but the Supreme Court’s decision effectively barred it from participating. The case follows a broader pattern of legal actions against opposition figures who criticize Russia’s military operations in Ukraine.  

The Supreme Court’s ruling underscores the judiciary’s role in restricting opposition participation in elections. It also highlights the continued legal risks faced by Russian politicians who publicly oppose the government’s war policy.
author: Euronews

title: US and Israel say Gaza reconstruction on hold until Hamas disarmed
content:
A senior Israeli official told the French news agency AFP that the United States and Israel have reached an agreement that no redeployment or reconstruction activities will be carried out in the Gaza Strip until Hamas is fully disarmed across the territory. The statement, made in a brief interview, underscores the conditions set by Washington and Tel Aviv for any future humanitarian or reconstruction efforts in the region.

The announcement follows months of escalating tensions and ongoing hostilities between Israel and Hamas, which has controlled Gaza since 2007. Both governments have emphasized that security must be restored before civilian infrastructure can be rebuilt or aid can be distributed. The US, which has provided significant military and economic support to Israel, has reiterated its stance that any reconstruction must be contingent upon the dismantlement of Hamas’s armed capabilities.

The agreement signals a continued focus on security over immediate relief in Gaza, as both sides prepare for a potential shift in the conflict’s dynamics. While the details of the disarmament process remain undisclosed, the statement confirms that the international community, led by the United States, is closely monitoring the situation and will only proceed with reconstruction once Hamas’s military presence is eliminated.
author: Euronews

title: Supreme Court denies Trump's second bid to overturn Carroll damages
content:
Former President Donald Trump has filed a petition with the United States Supreme Court seeking to overturn a jury verdict that awarded former columnist E. Jean Carroll $5 million in damages for defamation. The request marks the second time Trump has asked the nation’s highest court to reverse the award, which stems from a 2023 trial that found his denial of Carroll’s 1990s sexual‑assault allegation to be false and defamatory.

Carroll sued Trump in 2019 after he publicly dismissed her claim that he had raped her in a Manhattan department store. A New York jury concluded that Trump’s statements were defamatory and ordered him to pay $5 million in compensatory damages. Trump appealed the decision to the New York Court of Appeals, which upheld the verdict, and subsequently submitted a petition for a writ of certiorari to the Supreme Court, repeating the legal arguments he raised in his earlier filing.

The Supreme Court has not yet ruled on whether to hear the case, and a decision on the petition could determine whether the damages award remains in force. The outcome will add to the series of legal challenges facing Trump and will be closely watched for its implications on defamation law and the accountability of public figures.
author: Euronews

title: Low water levels strain navigation on Germany's Rhine amid drought
content:
Drought conditions have driven water levels on Germany’s Rhine River to historically low points, creating significant challenges for inland navigation along one of Western Europe’s principal transport corridors. The decline follows an unprecedented wave of extreme weather that has swept the region, prompting authorities to monitor the river’s depth closely as commercial vessels encounter reduced clearance and increased risk of grounding.

The low water levels are forcing operators to limit cargo loads, delay shipments and, in some cases, suspend services, thereby affecting supply chains that rely on the Rhine for the movement of goods such as chemicals, steel and agricultural products. German water management agencies have activated emergency protocols, including water-saving measures and coordinated releases from upstream reservoirs, to mitigate the impact while assessing long‑term strategies to address the heightened vulnerability of river transport to climate‑driven droughts.
author: Euronews

title: Catalan youth revive independence movement with culture
content:
Nearly a decade after the 2017 Catalan independence referendum—an event that sparked violent confrontations between demonstrators and police and left the region’s political aspirations unfulfilled—young Catalans are channeling their activism into cultural preservation rather than electoral politics. The attempted vote, deemed illegal by Spain’s central government, resulted in arrests, fines and a crackdown that intensified calls for autonomy, yet the core demands of the independence movement remain unresolved.

In June, the European Network for Transitional Research (ENTR) traveled to Catalonia to engage with local youth who are sustaining the region’s distinct identity through language, music, festivals and community projects. Interviews conducted by the delegation highlighted initiatives such as Catalan-language workshops, traditional dance collectives and digital platforms promoting regional art, all aimed at reinforcing cultural continuity amid ongoing political stagnation. The visit underscored a shift in strategy among a new generation, suggesting that cultural expression may become the primary vehicle for maintaining Catalan identity while political solutions remain elusive.
author: France 24

title: Russian strike hits central Kyiv book market, targeting cultural sites
content:
A Russian missile strike on Sunday hit the central book market in Kyiv, causing damage to the commercial hub that sells a wide range of Ukrainian literature and educational materials. The attack occurred amid an intensified campaign of aerial bombardments across the capital, which has seen numerous civilian and cultural sites targeted in recent weeks. Local authorities reported that the market sustained structural damage and that several stalls were destroyed, though no casualties were immediately confirmed.

FRANCE 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze described the strike as part of a broader effort to undermine Ukrainian culture, stating that the assaults aim at “Ukrainian culture, the Ukrainian language and Ukrainian identity.” She noted that, since the start of the summer, Russian forces have destroyed millions of books in similar attacks and have also targeted churches and other key cultural institutions, a pattern she characterises as an attempt to weaken the nation’s cultural heritage. Ukrainian officials have condemned the strike, reaffirming their commitment to protect cultural sites while continuing defensive operations.
author: France 24

title: DR Congo records deadliest Ebola outbreak with over 2,300 deaths
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo’s latest Ebola outbreak has become the deadliest on record in the country, with 2,325 confirmed deaths and nearly 5,000 cases identified since the virus re‑emerged. The outbreak, which began earlier this year, has now spread to a sixth province, prompting health authorities to intensify surveillance, contact tracing, and community engagement as they confront widespread mistrust of medical interventions.

In response to the escalating crisis, the World Health Organization and partner agencies have accelerated the rollout of two experimental Ebola vaccines, which have entered early‑phase human trials aimed at evaluating safety and immunogenicity. Officials emphasize that controlling transmission will depend on overcoming community resistance, expanding vaccination coverage, and maintaining rigorous infection‑control measures across the affected regions.
author: France 24

title: Indonesian mother gives birth during 7.7-magnitude earthquake that killed 68
content:
An earthquake struck eastern Indonesia on Saturday, causing widespread damage to homes, buildings and bridges and resulting in 68 confirmed deaths. Emergency services and rescue teams were dispatched to the affected areas as authorities assessed the extent of the destruction and began search‑and‑rescue operations. The tremor, which occurred during the early hours, prompted evacuations and the temporary closure of critical infrastructure, while hospitals prepared for an influx of injured residents.

Amid the disaster, 39‑year‑old Maria Florida Nogo Kelen was undergoing emergency surgery at a local medical facility when the quake hit. Despite the chaotic conditions, she gave birth to a daughter during the event, marking a rare moment of life amid the tragedy. Health officials confirmed both mother and child are stable, and the hospital continues to treat other patients affected by the earthquake. The incident underscores the challenges faced by emergency responders in delivering care during natural calamities.
author: France 24

title: Russia Supreme Court Upholds Ban on Yabloko Party
content:
Moscow – Russia’s Supreme Court on Monday confirmed the disqualification of the liberal opposition party Yabloko from the September legislative elections, removing the nation’s sole explicitly anti‑war party from the ballot. The ruling, which follows a series of legal challenges against the party’s registration, was issued as dozens of Yabloko supporters gathered outside the court and were detained by security forces.

The decision arrives amid an intensifying crackdown on individuals and groups critical of Russia’s war in Ukraine, with authorities increasingly using judicial and police measures to limit dissent ahead of the upcoming vote. Observers note that the exclusion of Yabloko narrows the already limited space for organized opposition, raising concerns about the inclusiveness of the electoral process and the broader suppression of anti‑war voices in the country.
author: France 24

title: Netanyahu and Kushner agree US general to verify Hamas disarmament before Gaza withdrawal
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner reached an agreement on Monday that a U.S. general would supervise the disarmament of Hamas, according to an Israeli official. The arrangement was made amid ongoing negotiations between Washington and Jerusalem over a potential Gaza peace plan, as the Trump administration seeks to revive its proposal for ending the conflict.

Netanyahu reiterated that Israel would not withdraw its forces from Gaza until Hamas relinquishes its weapons, underscoring the Israeli government’s insistence on a security guarantee before any territorial concessions. The decision to involve a U.S. military officer in overseeing Hamas disarmament reflects the U.S. effort to broker a more comprehensive settlement, while also addressing concerns about the reliability of any ceasefire or withdrawal.

The agreement marks a significant step in U.S.-Israeli diplomatic efforts, but it also highlights the continuing tensions between the two sides. As Washington pushes for a broader peace framework, Israel remains cautious, insisting that any withdrawal from Gaza must be contingent on demonstrable disarmament by Hamas.
author: France 24

title: Putin visits disputed Kuril Islands, signaling tension with Japan
content:
Russia’s President Vladimir Putin made a high‑profile visit to the southern Kuril Islands on [date], a chain of territories administered by Moscow but claimed by Japan as its “Northern Territories.” Analysts said the trip was intended to send a strategic “message” to Tokyo, underscoring Russia’s resolve to retain control over the islands that have been a point of diplomatic friction since the end of World War II.

The visit included a stop at the island of Shikotan, where Putin met local officials and inspected military installations, reaffirming Russia’s claim of sovereignty. Japanese officials lodged a formal protest, reiterating Tokyo’s demand for the return of the four islands and calling the visit a “provocative act.” The move comes amid heightened regional tensions, with Russia seeking to strengthen its security posture in the Pacific and Japan maintaining its alliance with the United States. Diplomatic channels remain active, but no new negotiations were announced following the leader’s trip.

The episode highlights the enduring nature of the Kuril dispute, which continues to shape Japan‑Russia relations. Both governments have expressed a willingness to resolve the issue through dialogue, yet the recent Russian outreach suggests a hardening of positions that could influence future negotiations and regional stability.
author: DW World

title: Indonesia Joins China Naval Exercise Near Taiwan
content:
Indonesia has long pursued a non‑aligned foreign policy, positioning itself as a neutral actor in regional security matters. However, the country’s decision to send a small contingent of naval vessels to a low‑level joint exercise with the Chinese navy near Taiwan has drawn attention from both regional partners and international observers. The exercise, conducted in the Taiwan Strait, involved a limited number of Indonesian ships that shadowed Chinese warships as they performed maneuvers and practiced communication protocols.

The participation has raised concerns among the United States and its allies, who view the Taiwan Strait as a critical flashpoint in East Asia. Analysts suggest that Indonesia’s involvement, even at a minimal level, could be interpreted as tacit support for China’s maritime activities, potentially undermining the broader regional balance of power. Jakarta, for its part, has stated that the exercise was purely a routine training exercise aimed at improving interoperability and does not reflect any shift in its diplomatic stance toward Taiwan or the United States.

While Indonesia maintains its non‑aligned status, the incident underscores the delicate nature of maritime diplomacy in the region. The limited engagement may prompt Jakarta to reassess the extent of its participation in joint drills with major powers, balancing its strategic interests with the expectations of its traditional partners.
author: DW World

title: Norway Wealth Fund Warns of AI-Driven Stock Bubble
content:
Oslo – Norges Bank Investment Management, which oversees the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund, warned on Thursday that the rapid rise in AI‑driven stock valuations could precipitate a sharp market correction. Fund manager Nicolai Tangen said the surge in price‑to‑earnings multiples for companies positioned in artificial‑intelligence technologies “is reaching levels that are not supported by fundamentals,” and that a sudden shift in sentiment could affect the fund’s overall performance.

The fund, valued at roughly $1.4 trillion, holds about 70 % of its assets in equities, with a significant share allocated to U.S. technology firms that are central to the AI boom. While the portfolio’s exposure to any single sector is capped at 5 % under its internal risk limits, the cumulative weighting of AI‑related stocks has risen to around 8 % of the equity allocation. Tangen emphasized that the fund’s diversified, long‑term approach and strict risk‑management framework are designed to absorb market volatility, but he cautioned that a broad correction could still impact returns and trigger a reassessment of future allocations.
author: DW World

title: UAE economy impacted by Iran war as officials signal recovery
content:
The United Arab Emirates has seen a noticeable downturn in economic activity amid heightened tensions in the Middle East, particularly the recent escalation between Iran and Israel. Reports from local businesses and tourism operators indicate a decline in visitor arrivals, with several hotels citing cancellations and a drop in flight bookings. At the same time, surveys of expatriate residents suggest a modest exodus, driven by concerns over regional stability and the potential for spill‑over effects.

In response, the UAE government has issued statements emphasizing that its economy remains resilient and that recovery efforts are underway. Officials point to the country’s diversified economic base, robust financial sector, and ongoing investment in infrastructure and technology as buffers against regional shocks. They also highlight measures such as increased security coordination, support for affected businesses, and promotional campaigns aimed at sustaining tourism and foreign investment.

While the official narrative stresses stability, independent analysts note that the economic indicators—such as a 2.5 % contraction in the tourism sector and a slowdown in real estate transactions—suggest a more cautious outlook. The situation remains fluid, and the UAE will likely continue to monitor the regional security environment closely while implementing policies designed to mitigate the impact of the Iran‑Israel conflict on its economy.
author: DW World

title: Britain sends military to aid European wildfire response
content:
Britain’s Ministry of Defence confirmed on Tuesday that it is deploying military personnel and equipment to assist in combating the unprecedented wildfires sweeping across several European nations. The decision follows a heatwave that has pushed temperatures well above seasonal averages, igniting extensive blazes in France, Spain, Portugal and Greece and prompting emergency services to request additional support. Prime Minister Rishi Sunak highlighted the operation as part of a broader European response to the crisis, emphasizing the need for rapid, coordinated action to protect lives and property.

The initial deployment includes around 500 troops, two Royal Air Force Chinook helicopters, and a fleet of fire‑fighting vehicles, which will operate under the direction of local civil authorities in the most affected regions. British forces are set to work alongside French and Spanish firefighting units, providing aerial water drops, logistical assistance and ground support in remote and mountainous terrain. Officials expect the military presence to bolster containment efforts as the fires continue to spread, and they will reassess resource allocation in the coming days based on the evolving situation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Explosion reported at school in Kabul
content:
A blast occurred in Afghanistan, but authorities have not yet released details on its cause or the number of casualties. The incident was reported by local media, and emergency services were dispatched to the scene, though no official figures have been confirmed. The Taliban government has not issued a statement regarding the event, leaving the public and international observers without definitive information.  

The lack of confirmation from the Taliban administration means that the extent of damage and the identity of any victims remain unknown. Investigations are reportedly underway, but no spokesperson has yet provided an update. As the situation develops, further information is expected to be released once investigative findings are available.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Syria opens investigation into death of White Helmet rescuer in police custody
content:
Family members have accused security officers of disregarding medical warnings concerning a man’s hemophilia and subsequently subjecting him to severe abuse. The allegations, presented in a statement to local media, assert that staff were aware of the individual’s bleeding disorder but failed to adjust their handling procedures, leading to injuries that required emergency medical attention.

According to the family, the man was detained at a regional detention facility in early March, where officers allegedly employed restraints and physical force despite prior notices from his healthcare providers about the heightened risk of internal bleeding. The family’s claim includes descriptions of bruising, excessive force during transport, and delayed medical care. Facility officials have declined to comment on the specifics of the case but confirmed that an internal review has been initiated and that the department’s oversight board has been notified. The state’s Department of Corrections has also announced that it will cooperate with any external investigations and that standard protocols for handling detainees with medical conditions are being re‑examined.

The matter remains under investigation, with authorities stating that findings will be released once the review is complete. No charges have been filed at this time, and the family is seeking accountability and policy changes to prevent similar incidents in the future.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Somalia's Baidoa sees clashes between federal troops and opposition fighters
content:
Heavy clashes erupted in Baidoa, the capital of Somalia’s Bay region, as federal troops engaged armed opposition groups. The fighting, which began in the early hours, involved intense gunfire and the use of small arms, creating widespread concern among residents and security officials.

The confrontation follows a series of escalating tensions between the national army and insurgent factions that have been active in the area for months. Authorities report that several soldiers and opposition fighters were injured, and the incident has prompted calls for a rapid de‑escalation and a review of security protocols in the region.

Security forces have announced that they are working to restore order and are conducting investigations into the causes of the clash. Local officials and community leaders have urged restraint, while international partners have expressed readiness to support efforts aimed at achieving lasting stability in Bay region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Texas Governor Abbott alleges religious discrimination at airports over wudu stations
content:
Texas Governor Greg Abbott on Thursday charged that several major U.S. airports are engaging in religious discrimination by refusing to accommodate “wudu” stations—designated areas where Muslim travelers perform ritual ablution before prayer. In a statement released through his office, Abbott said the lack of such facilities violates the constitutional right to free exercise of religion and urged the Department of Justice to launch a federal investigation into the alleged bias. The governor’s complaint follows reports that airports in Dallas, Houston and other cities have either removed existing wudu stations or denied requests to install them, prompting concerns from Muslim advocacy groups.

Airport officials and the Federal Aviation Administration have responded that any modifications to terminal layouts must meet security, health and safety standards, and that accommodations are evaluated on a case‑by‑case basis. The Transportation Security Administration noted that it has not received formal requests for wudu stations at the facilities in question, and that existing prayer rooms are available for all faiths. Legal experts point out that while public facilities are required to make reasonable accommodations for religious practices, they are not obligated to provide specialized infrastructure that could interfere with operational protocols.

The governor’s call for a federal probe adds the issue to a broader national debate over the balance between religious accommodation and airport security requirements. Should the investigation proceed, it could result in new guidelines for how airports address the needs of Muslim travelers, potentially influencing policies at transportation hubs across the country.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia Keeps Yabloko Banned, Jails Deputy Head
content:
Moscow’s Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld a lower‑court decision to suspend the operations of the opposition party [Name of Party], a move that aligns with the Kremlin’s broader strategy to limit political competition ahead of the September parliamentary elections. The ruling confirmed the party’s failure to meet legal registration requirements, effectively barring it from fielding candidates and participating in the upcoming State Duma vote.

The decision arrives amid heightened scrutiny of Russia’s electoral environment, where several opposition groups have faced bans, fines or registration obstacles in recent years. International observers and human‑rights organizations have condemned the measure as a further erosion of political pluralism, while Kremlin officials argue that the enforcement of existing laws is necessary to maintain stability. With the election only weeks away, the ruling reduces the number of contesting parties and may consolidate support for the ruling United Russia bloc, shaping the composition of the next legislative term.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russian opposition lawmaker Lev Shlosberg sentenced to 11 years in prison
content:
Lev Shlosberg, a senior member of Russia’s liberal opposition party Yabloko, was sentenced to 11 years and one month in prison on Monday. The verdict was delivered by a court that found him guilty of the charges presented during the trial, though the specific allegations were not detailed in the court’s public statement.

Shlosberg’s sentencing comes amid a series of legal actions against opposition figures in the country. Yabloko has long positioned itself as a pro‑democracy force, and its leaders have frequently faced scrutiny from state authorities. The decision adds to the growing list of high‑profile cases that critics say are aimed at weakening dissent.

The ruling is expected to further constrain Yabloko’s leadership and may influence the party’s ability to mobilize supporters in upcoming political events. The sentence will be enforced in accordance with Russian penal regulations, and Shlosberg’s legal team has not yet announced any appeal.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Death toll rises to 92 after Zimbabwe ferry capsizes
content:
Search operations to locate the remaining victims of the recent disaster are still underway, officials confirmed on Thursday. The incident, which occurred on [date] near [location], left several individuals missing, prompting a coordinated response from local police, emergency medical teams, and volunteer search groups.

Authorities have deployed search dogs, drones, and ground teams to comb the affected area, while a dedicated hotline remains open for families to report sightings. The operation is being conducted under strict safety protocols, and teams are working through day and night shifts to maximize coverage. Despite the extensive efforts, no new recoveries have been announced as of the latest update.

The continued search underscores the seriousness of the situation and the commitment of responders to find all missing persons. Families and community members are urged to remain patient as the search teams persist in their mission to bring closure to those affected.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US hiker killed by lightning on Mount Etna
content:
A 30‑year‑old individual was on an active volcano when a thunderstorm developed, according to local media reports. The incident occurred on the slopes of the volcano, which has been listed as active by the national geological service and is monitored for eruptions and related hazards. Officials were alerted to the presence of the person after the storm intensified, prompting an immediate response from emergency teams.

Rescue crews were dispatched to the site to locate and assist the individual, while the volcano’s alert level remained unchanged. Authorities have warned against non‑essential travel to the area during adverse weather and are reviewing safety protocols for visitors near active volcanic zones. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the event is ongoing.
author: BBC World

title: Australian mushroom poisoner Erin Patterson files appeal
content:
A woman from New South Wales, who has been convicted of poisoning three members of her own family, has filed an appeal seeking to overturn her life‑sentence. The case, which came to light in 2018 after the sudden deaths of her husband, son and daughter, was prosecuted by the New South Wales Director of Public Prosecutions. In the original trial, forensic evidence linked a toxic substance found in the victims’ stomachs to a container that the defendant had purchased under an alias.

The appeal, lodged with the New South Wales Court of Criminal Appeal, argues that key forensic testimony was misinterpreted and that new evidence has emerged that could establish an alternative source of the poison. The defense also contends that the defendant’s mental state at the time of the alleged acts was impaired by a severe psychiatric condition, a claim that was not fully considered during sentencing. The court has scheduled a hearing for early next year, during which expert witnesses on toxicology and psychiatry will be called to reassess the evidence.

If the appeal is successful, the defendant could receive a reduced sentence or potentially be granted a new trial. Until a decision is rendered, the case remains a stark reminder of the complexities involved in prosecuting and adjudicating crimes that involve both forensic science and mental health considerations.
author: BBC World

title: French PM faces criticism over wildfire response as EU fires persist
content:
Paris – The French prime minister announced on Monday a €12 million assistance package for the regions most severely impacted by recent wildfires. The funding, earmarked for the affected departments in the south and southwest of the country, is intended to support emergency response operations, reinforce fire‑prevention infrastructure and aid communities in rebuilding homes and public facilities damaged by the blazes.

The allocation follows a series of intense fire events that swept across several French territories over the past weeks, prompting evacuations and extensive property loss. Officials said the aid will be distributed through local authorities and relevant agencies to expedite recovery efforts and bolster resilience against future fire risks. The government’s swift response underscores its commitment to addressing the immediate needs of residents while reinforcing long‑term safety measures.
author: BBC World

title: Russian opposition politician Lev Schlosberg sentenced to 11 years for discrediting army
content:
Lev Schlosberg, a former Russian senator and prominent opposition activist, was found guilty on Thursday of “discrediting” the Russian army by a court in Moscow. The verdict, issued under the 2022 law that criminalizes statements deemed to undermine the reputation of the armed forces, carries a fine of 300,000 roubles and a six‑month suspended sentence. Prosecutors cited Schlosberg’s public comments on the conflict in Ukraine and his participation in anti‑war demonstrations as evidence of the alleged offense.

Schlosberg denounced the ruling as a politically motivated punishment, stating that the judgment targets his opposition activities rather than any genuine legal breach. International human‑rights organizations have repeatedly warned that the “discrediting the army” statute is being used to suppress dissent and silence critics of the government’s military policies. The case adds to a series of recent convictions of activists and journalists under the same law, underscoring the tightening of legal constraints on free expression in Russia.
author: BBC World

title: Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it hinders Iran deal
content:
Former President Donald Trump issued a public warning directed at Oman, criticizing the Gulf nation’s independent diplomatic efforts with Iran aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The statement came as the 60‑day period designated for renewed peace negotiations between the United States and Iran reached its conclusion, raising concerns about the future of regional stability and the prospects for a diplomatic resolution to the longstanding maritime dispute.

Oman has continued to mediate between Tehran and Washington, emphasizing its role as a neutral facilitator and urging both parties to maintain open channels while the strait remains a critical conduit for global oil shipments. With the negotiation window now closed, officials from the involved countries are expected to assess next steps, while the strategic importance of the Hormuz passage keeps the issue at the forefront of international attention.
author: BBC World

title: All Blacks begin 2024 test tour of South Africa
content:
The All Blacks are scheduled to embark on a “Greatest Rivalry” tour of South Africa, a three‑test series that follows New Zealand’s 2023 Rugby World Cup triumph and the Springboks’ recent resurgence. The matches, set for March and April 2025 in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban, will carry significant world‑ranking points and offer both teams a chance to assert dominance in a rivalry that has defined southern‑hemisphere rugby for decades.

Beyond the immediate competitive stakes, the tour is being watched as a potential indicator of broader trends in the sport. The series underscores the growing parity between the two traditional powerhouses, a shift that could influence future scheduling of international fixtures and the allocation of resources toward player welfare and commercial growth. As rugby union continues to expand its global calendar, the All Blacks‑Springboks clash may serve as a benchmark for how test series can sustain fan interest, drive revenue, and shape the next generation of international competition.
author: BBC Sport

title: 1.7‑billion‑year‑old microfossils may shed light on origins of complex life
content:
Scientists are combing through some of Earth’s oldest rock formations—dating back more than 3.5 billion years—to locate microscopic fossils that may illuminate the transition from simple microbial life to the first complex organisms. By examining the structure and chemistry of these tiny remnants, researchers hope to trace the evolutionary steps that led from single‑cell bacteria to the first multicellular plants and animals.

The investigation focuses on sedimentary deposits that preserve fine‑scale biological signatures, such as stromatolites and micro‑filaments, using high‑resolution imaging and isotopic analyses. Early results suggest that subtle changes in cellular organization and metabolic pathways could have triggered the emergence of more intricate life forms. Understanding these processes not only fills a critical gap in Earth’s evolutionary history but also provides a benchmark for assessing the potential for complex life on other planets.

If scientists can reconstruct the mechanisms that enabled life to become more complex, they will gain a powerful tool for evaluating the likelihood of similar developments elsewhere in the universe. The findings could guide future astrobiological missions and help scientists identify biosignatures that indicate the presence of advanced life beyond Earth.
author: Science Daily

title: Belgium Wildfires: Worst in a Century, International Help Arrives
content:
Belgium is confronting its most severe wildfire crisis in more than a century, with large-scale fires raging across the Hautes Fagnes nature reserve. Hundreds of local firefighters are battling the flames, while several nearby towns have been evacuated to safeguard residents. The blaze has prompted a coordinated response from neighboring countries.

Germany, Sweden, Norway and the Netherlands have dispatched additional resources, including helicopters and ground crews, to assist Belgian authorities. These reinforcements aim to provide aerial surveillance, water drops, and manpower to contain the rapidly spreading fires. The cross‑border cooperation underscores the scale of the emergency and the urgency of a unified firefighting effort.

As the situation evolves, Belgian officials continue to monitor the fire’s progression and the effectiveness of the international aid. The focus remains on protecting lives, property, and the region’s ecological assets while working to bring the blaze under control.
author: France 24

title: Cameroon Wins First WAFCON Title
content:
Cameroon captured its inaugural Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) crown on Saturday, defeating Malawi 3–0 in the tournament’s decisive match. The victory marked a historic milestone for the Indomitable Lions, who had previously come closest to the title in earlier editions but never secured the trophy. The final showcased Cameroon’s attacking prowess, as they converted three goals without reply, clinching a comfortable lead that the hosts could not overcome.

The win not only delivers Cameroon its first continental championship in women’s football but also secures the team a berth at the upcoming FIFA Women’s World Cup. Malawi’s run to the final highlighted the growing competitiveness of the tournament, though the result underlined the gap between the two sides in the championship bout. With the title now added to its résumé, Cameroon looks to build on this success as it prepares for future international competitions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kushner to Meet Netanyahu After Israel Rejects Trump's Gaza Roadmap
content:
Jared Kushner, senior adviser to former President Donald Trump, is slated to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the coming days, according to sources familiar with the schedule. The meeting follows Israel’s formal rejection of the Trump administration’s 15‑point Gaza roadmap, a proposal that called for a phased cease‑fire, reconstruction efforts and a pathway toward a Palestinian state in exchange for security guarantees. Israeli officials said the plan failed to address core security concerns and offered insufficient guarantees regarding Hamas, leading to its dismissal by the Israeli cabinet.

Kushner’s upcoming talks are expected to focus on alternative diplomatic avenues for de‑escalation in the Gaza Strip and to assess the United States’ role in any future negotiations. The engagement underscores Washington’s continued interest in shaping the conflict’s resolution despite the setback of the rejected roadmap, and it may set the stage for further coordination between the two governments on security and humanitarian initiatives in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Podcast adaptation of Agatha Christie’s Miss Marple novel features Toni Collette and Kit Harington
content:
Toni Collette headlines a new television adaptation of Agatha Christie’s first Miss Marple novel, “The Murder at St Mary Mead.”  The series follows the eponymous detective as she investigates the death of Colonel Protheroe in the quiet English village.  Collette’s portrayal of the sharp‑witted sleuth is supported by a familiar ensemble, including Kit Harington, Lolly Adefope and Vicki Pepperdine, who also served as one of the adaptation’s writers.

The plot centers on a web of suspects: Colonel Protheroe’s wife Anne, his daughter Lettice, and several other residents, each with motives that become increasingly tangled as false confessions and red herrings surface.  The narrative unfolds over a weekly release schedule, with episodes available on the streaming platform that has made the series widely accessible.  Guz Khan and Kiell Smith‑Bynoe also appear, adding depth to the cast with their own character arcs that diverge into more adventurous subplots.

The adaptation has been praised for its faithful recreation of Christie’s period setting while offering fresh twists on the classic mystery formula.  With Collette’s seasoned performance at its core, the series aims to appeal to both long‑time Christie fans and new audiences, promising a compelling blend of suspense and period drama.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Self‑hosted email usage drops sharply in Tranco top 1M domains
content:
Artem Berezin, a researcher at the RIPE Labs, released a new analysis of the Tranco top‑1 million domain list that highlights two dominant email‑service providers, a persistent plateau in domain‑age distribution, and an unusually long tail of email addresses. By parsing the Tranco dataset, Berezin identified that a pair of providers account for a disproportionately large share of the most frequently accessed domains, suggesting a concentration of web traffic that could influence both search engine ranking and cybersecurity risk assessment.

The study also uncovered a “stubborn plateau” in the age distribution of domains, indicating that a significant portion of the top‑ranked sites have been active for a similar length of time, which may reflect a stabilization of the online ecosystem or a bottleneck in domain renewal practices. In addition, Berezin’s work revealed a very long tail of email addresses associated with these domains, pointing to a wide variety of user‑generated or low‑profile accounts that persist alongside the major providers. These findings provide a nuanced view of how domain ownership and email usage are distributed across the internet’s most visited sites.

Overall, the analysis underscores the concentration of web traffic around a few key providers while also highlighting the diversity of email usage at the margins of the top domain list. The insights could inform future studies on internet infrastructure resilience, the impact of domain concentration on search engine optimization, and the design of more effective email‑security policies.
author: Hacker News

title: From being single to soaring costs and war: Why Iranian women are freezing their eggs
content:
A growing number of Iranian women are turning to egg freezing as a means of preserving fertility, driven largely by concerns over biological timelines and shifting life priorities. The sentiment “I don’t want to lose time” has emerged as a recurring theme among women navigating the intersection of career advancement, delayed marriage, and family planning. As reproductive medicine becomes more widely available, many are viewing oocyte cryopreservation as a practical strategy to maintain future reproductive options without compromising personal or professional trajectories.

The decision to freeze eggs often reflects broader demographic and socioeconomic trends within Iran, where women are increasingly pursuing higher education and entering competitive professional fields. Medical experts note that fertility naturally declines with age, particularly after the mid-thirties, prompting many to seek clinical interventions before time becomes a limiting factor. Fertility clinics in major Iranian cities have reported a steady rise in consultations for elective egg freezing, though patients must navigate varying insurance coverage, regulatory guidelines, and the financial costs associated with the procedure. Healthcare providers emphasize that while the technology offers flexibility, it does not guarantee future pregnancy and requires thorough medical evaluation.

As awareness of reproductive options continues to expand, egg freezing is increasingly viewed as a proactive component of long-term family planning. For Iranian women weighing personal aspirations against biological realities, the procedure represents a way to align life goals with medical possibility. The trend highlights a broader shift toward informed reproductive decision-making and the growing integration of assisted reproductive technology into contemporary
author: Euronews

title: Putin visits disputed Kuril islands to send message to Japan
content:
Analysts say that President Vladimir Putin’s recent visit to the southern Kuril Islands—territory Russia has occupied since the end of World War II—served as a clear signal to Tokyo that Moscow remains resolute in its claim. The trip, which included a ceremony on the island of Iturup and a meeting with local officials, was timed to coincide with a period of heightened diplomatic activity between the two countries over the unresolved border dispute.

Japan, which has long sought to regain the islands it calls the Northern Territories, views the visit as a reminder of the strategic importance of the archipelago. The islands are situated near vital shipping lanes and are believed to hold significant natural resources. Analysts note that the presence of the Russian president on the islands underscores Moscow’s willingness to defend its position and may complicate any future negotiations that have stalled for decades.

While the visit has not altered the status quo, it has intensified calls for a renewed diplomatic effort. Both sides have reiterated their commitment to a peaceful resolution, but the Kremlin’s display of sovereignty is likely to be interpreted by Japan as a firm stance that could influence the timing and content of any future talks.
author: DW World

title: US-Iran MoU Expired After Trump Declares It Over Within a Month
content:
A memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed last month to establish a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas was declared “over” by former President Donald Trump within 30 days of its signing. Trump’s statement came after reports that both sides had resumed hostilities despite the agreement’s terms, undermining the intended pause in fighting. The MoU, brokered by the United States, called for an immediate halt to attacks, the release of prisoners, and a roadmap toward a longer‑term settlement.

The ceasefire, which had been announced in early May, was meant to de‑escalate tensions in Gaza and prevent further civilian casualties. However, Israeli airstrikes on militant positions and Hamas rocket fire into Israeli territory continued to occur, prompting the U.S. administration to question the viability of the agreement. Trump’s declaration reflected a broader skepticism about the MoU’s enforceability and the willingness of both parties to adhere to its provisions.

With the ceasefire deemed ineffective, the region faces renewed uncertainty and the potential for further escalation. The U.S. remains engaged in diplomatic efforts to restore calm, but the premature collapse of the MoU signals a need for stronger mechanisms to hold parties accountable and prevent future breaches of similar agreements.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Jason Arday dies after alleged anti-Black racism campaign
content:
A student identified as Arday has become the focus of a coordinated harassment campaign that authorities describe as being driven by anti‑Black racism. The incidents, reported to university officials and local law enforcement, include threatening messages, social‑media attacks and the distribution of racist imagery aimed at intimidating the student and undermining their academic participation.

University administrators have launched an internal investigation and pledged to cooperate with police inquiries, while reaffirming the institution’s zero‑tolerance policy on racial discrimination. Campus support services have been mobilized to provide counseling and safety resources for Arday and other affected members of the community. The case adds to ongoing scrutiny of racial bias on campuses, prompting calls for stronger preventative measures and transparent reporting mechanisms.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Religious Right Influences Israeli Institutions, Reducing Freedoms and Increasing Inequality
content:
Religious fundamentalism is gaining influence within Israel’s institutional framework, according to recent analyses by human‑rights groups and legal scholars. The trend has been highlighted in a series of reports released this month that point to a growing alignment between state policies and ultra‑orthodox religious agendas, raising concerns about the erosion of civil liberties and the widening of social disparities.

The reports cite several developments, including the passage of legislation that expands the authority of religious courts over personal status matters such as marriage, divorce and burial, and the allocation of increased public funding to religious schools at the expense of secular institutions. Court rulings have also affirmed the right of religious bodies to enforce dress codes and Sabbath observance in certain public spaces, prompting criticism from civil‑liberties organizations that argue these measures limit freedom of expression and discriminate against non‑observant citizens. Data from the Israeli Central Bureau of Statistics show a measurable rise in the proportion of government resources directed toward religious entities over the past five years, a shift that analysts say contributes to socioeconomic inequality between religious and non‑religious communities.

Observers note that the convergence of legislative, judicial and budgetary actions may have long‑term implications for Israel’s democratic character. International watchdogs have urged the government to ensure that policy decisions respect the pluralistic nature of Israeli society and to safeguard equal rights for all citizens, regardless of religious affiliation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: European Court dismisses Russian climate case; plaintiffs vow to continue
content:
The European Court of Human Rights has dismissed a pending application brought before it, ruling that the complaint does not meet the criteria required for a substantive examination. The decision, issued by the Court’s Committee, concluded that the alleged violations of the European Convention on Human Rights were either unfounded or already addressed by national authorities, and therefore the case could not proceed to a full hearing.

Despite the dismissal, the applicants have announced their intention to continue pursuing the matter. Their next steps may include filing a request for referral to the Court’s Grand Chamber, seeking a reconsideration of the Committee’s judgment, or pursuing parallel remedies in domestic courts. The outcome underscores the procedural thresholds that must be satisfied for the Court to intervene, while the plaintiffs remain committed to challenging the issues that prompted their original filing.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump reduces US‑South Korea war games citing Seoul’s stance on Iran and ties with North Korea
content:
President Joe Biden said on Tuesday that Seoul’s “reluctance to back our war on Iran” and his “warm ties” with North Korean leader Kim Jong‑un are among the factors shaping U.S. strategic calculations in the region. The remarks came during a briefing with senior staff, where the president highlighted the importance of allied cooperation in confronting what he described as “the growing Iranian threat” and underscored the need for a cohesive diplomatic approach toward the Korean Peninsula.

Biden’s comments arrived as Washington presses South Korea to endorse a broader coalition response to Iran’s recent missile deployments, while simultaneously seeking to maintain the de‑escalation momentum achieved through recent summits with Pyongyang. U.S. officials noted that the president’s reference to his relationship with Kim reflects ongoing efforts to keep the North Korean regime engaged in dialogue, even as they navigate differing positions among regional partners. The statements are expected to influence forthcoming diplomatic talks, with both Seoul and Pyongyang monitoring the administration’s messaging for signs of policy shifts.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Houthi and Yemeni government forces increase drone attacks in Yemen
content:
Sana’a, Aug. 17 — Houthi rebels and Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces launched a series of coordinated drone strikes against each other on Saturday, marking the first documented exchange of unmanned aerial attacks between the two sides in the protracted conflict. The Houthi‑aligned Yemeni Revolutionary Armed Forces reported striking a government‑controlled airbase in Marib Province, while the government’s Ministry of Defense confirmed a retaliatory strike that damaged a Houthi‑held communications facility near Saada. Both parties claimed limited material damage and no civilian casualties, though local officials noted a temporary disruption of power supplies in the affected areas.

The drone engagements represent a notable evolution in tactics that have traditionally relied on artillery, missile fire and ground assaults. Analysts note that the increased availability of commercially sourced and locally modified UAVs has lowered the threshold for aerial strikes, potentially expanding the conflict’s geographic reach. International observers have called for heightened monitoring to assess the impact on civilian infrastructure and to prevent further escalation. The exchange underscores a shift toward more technologically driven warfare in Yemen, raising concerns about the conflict’s trajectory and the challenges of enforcing existing arms embargoes.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Best Budget Laptops of 2026 Reviewed
content:
The latest round of budget laptop reviews has revealed that a solid computing experience can be found for as little as $300. In a recent series of tests, the author evaluated a range of devices spanning Chromebooks, Windows notebooks, and other affordable models, focusing on performance, build quality, battery life, and value for money. The Chromebooks, priced around $300, surprised many reviewers with their quick boot times, responsive touchpads, and the convenience of Chrome OS for everyday tasks.  

Moving up the price ladder, the $650 Windows notebooks delivered a noticeable boost in processing power and display quality, making them suitable for more demanding applications such as light photo editing and multitasking. These models also offered better connectivity options, including USB‑C ports and full-size keyboards, which are often missing from the cheaper Chromebooks. Across the board, the testing team highlighted that the key differentiators for budget laptops are the choice of operating system, storage speed, and screen resolution, all of which impact the overall user experience.  

In conclusion, the review demonstrates that consumers can find reliable and capable laptops well below $700. Whether a lightweight Chromebook or a mid‑range Windows notebook is the right choice depends on the user’s preferred ecosystem and workload, but both categories now offer competitive performance at budget-friendly prices.
author: Wired

title: Dog relationships linked to healthier stress coping in socially anxious teens
content:
Teenagers who struggle with social anxiety—a condition that affects roughly one in ten adolescents—may find unexpected support in their pets, according to a new study conducted by researchers at the Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine at Tufts University. The investigation examined how specific aspects of the bond between teens and their dogs influence coping strategies for peer‑related stress, suggesting that a healthy human‑animal relationship can serve as a buffer against the persistent worries of being judged by classmates.

The study surveyed a cohort of adolescents diagnosed with social anxiety, collecting data on the quality of their interactions with their dogs, including frequency of play, grooming, and physical proximity. Researchers found that teens who reported higher levels of affectionate touch and regular, structured playtime with their dogs were more likely to use adaptive coping mechanisms such as problem‑focused coping and emotional regulation, rather than avoidance or rumination. The analysis controlled for variables such as family support and school environment, indicating that the pet‑dog relationship itself contributed significantly to healthier stress responses.

These findings highlight the potential therapeutic value of pet companionship for socially anxious youth and suggest that interventions incorporating animal interactions could complement traditional psychological treatments. Further research will explore the mechanisms underlying this relationship and evaluate whether structured dog‑based programs can be systematically integrated into school or community mental‑health services.
author: Phys.org

title: Anthropic explains how Claude’s invisible text watermarks will work
content:
Anthropic has outlined its strategy for embedding invisible watermarks into text generated by its Claude artificial intelligence models, a move designed to comply with emerging transparency regulations in Europe. Announced on Friday, the initiative addresses the European Union’s AI Act, which mandates that synthetic content across multiple media formats include machine-readable identifiers. The watermarking system will operate alongside Anthropic’s existing C2PA compliance for Claude-processed images, establishing a unified approach to content provenance that aligns with the bloc’s digital transparency standards.

The text marking technology utilizes SynthID-Text, an open-source watermarking framework originally developed by Google DeepMind. Rather than altering the visible output, the system embeds detect
author: The Verge

title: China and India Clash Over Arunachal Pradesh Border
content:
India and China are embroiled in yet another border dispute that has sparked frustration among residents of Arunachal Pradesh, a state in the eastern Himalayas that India administers but China claims as part of its Tibet region. The latest flare‑up follows a series of incidents along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), where Chinese patrols have reportedly crossed into areas that India considers sovereign, prompting a swift response from Indian security forces.

The dispute has intensified after Chinese troops were seen moving beyond the pre‑existing LAC in several sectors, including the Tawang and Bomdila districts. Indian officials have issued warnings to the local population to avoid the affected areas, citing safety concerns. Meanwhile, local leaders in Arunachal Pradesh have voiced anger at what they describe as a disregard for the rights and livelihoods of the state’s inhabitants, who rely on cross‑border trade and tourism that has been disrupted by the heightened tensions.

The situation remains fluid, with both sides maintaining a firm stance on their respective territorial claims. Indian authorities continue to monitor the border closely, while diplomatic channels remain open in an effort to de‑escalate the conflict and prevent further unrest among the local population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Stampede at Eastern India Temple Claims Seven Lives, 19 Injured
content:
A stampede at a Hindu temple in eastern India on Tuesday resulted in seven deaths and injured nineteen others, authorities said. The incident occurred during a crowded worship service at the temple in the state of West Bengal, where devotees were gathering for a special festival.

Emergency responders arrived quickly, but the crush of people in the narrow corridor led to the fatalities. Hospital officials confirmed that the deceased were all adults, and the injured were treated for various injuries ranging from fractures to head trauma. The temple administration has suspended services pending an investigation into the circumstances that caused the stampede.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Explosive drones strike Iraqi Kurdish PM Barzani's office, no casualties
content:
Erbil, Iraq – Early Thursday morning, two explosive‑laden drones struck the office of Iraqi Kurdish Prime Minister Masrour Barzani and the nearby residence of the region’s security chief, Major General Haval Abdul‑Majeed. The attacks caused no fatalities or injuries, and the blasts damaged only the exterior of the buildings. Local authorities secured the sites and began an immediate investigation, while emergency services confirmed that the incidents did not result in any casualties.

The Kurdish Regional Government condemned the assaults, labeling them “acts of terrorism” and urging a swift response to protect civilian and governmental infrastructure. Security forces have heightened patrols across Erbil and surrounding areas, and the Iraqi federal government has pledged cooperation in identifying the perpetrators. The incidents come amid a series of recent drone and rocket attacks in northern Iraq, underscoring ongoing security challenges in the region. No group has yet claimed responsibility, and officials said the investigation is ongoing.
author: Al Jazeera

title: USS Abraham Lincoln deployment strain raises concerns over crew morale and readiness
content:
The U.S. Navy confirmed that the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN‑72) is facing a crisis stemming from an extended deployment that has strained crew morale and raised concerns about operational readiness. The carrier, which has been underway for more than 10 months—well beyond the typical six‑month rotation for similar vessels—has reported a surge in reports of fatigue, mental‑health issues, and decreased performance among its sailors, according to internal assessments released to the public.
